doc.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018

chapter: Howard Johnson and the loft scene
title: Howard Johnson as graduate school; jazz in school and constant practice
summary: Johnson was Daley's jazz education since schools offered little; he practiced through lunch at Music and Art.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well Howard Johnson was like your graduate school.

Oh yeah. He was my graduate school for jazz. Because jazz wasn’t taught in Manhattan School of Music at that particular time. Jazz wasn’t taught in my junior high school. Now my high school, we had a jazz program but it just had started. And I was fortunate enough to — in high school I never went to lunch. Because you know they had band classes all day. We had eight bands, we had eight orchestras, we had jazz ensemble, brass ensembles and everything. So any time there was a lunch period I would find where there was a band going on and I would sit in with that band or a brass ensemble, or I would find a practice room to practice. So I never ate lunch in the cafeteria. I practiced just about all the time. I have to get back to traveling.
